assumptions.choice: Opening-range high/low and day/bar-of-day bookkeeping are updated in prenext() as well as next(), so the first trading day's 4-bar range is still captured correctly even though backtrader delays next() until all indicators (SMA(volume,20) needs 20 bars) reach minperiod.
assumptions.reason: Canonical default #6 relies on automatic minperiod for next(), but without also tracking session state in prenext(), day 1's opening range window would be silently missed since next() would not start until well after bar 4.

assumptions.choice: The trailamount for the StopTrail order is computed from ATR(14) at the bar the entry order fills (inside notify_order), then fixed for that order per backtrader's StopTrail semantics.
assumptions.reason: Backtrader's StopTrail order takes a static trailamount at submission; ATR is a moving value, so the spec's 'trail amount = 1.5*ATR(14)' is read as sampled once at trade entry, which is the only point backtrader allows it to be fixed.

assumptions.topic: RSI momentum-stall exit vs. opposite-signal exit during opening-range formation
assumptions.choice: RSI(14) cross-through-50 exit is evaluated every in-session bar regardless of whether the current day's opening range is finalized; the opposite-breakout exit (and new entries) are only evaluated once the day's opening range is finalized.
assumptions.reason: The RSI condition has no stated dependency on the opening range, while the opposite-breakout condition and entries are explicitly defined in terms of the opening range, which is undefined during a day's first 4 bars (relevant if a position carries into a new session).

assumptions.choice: Added an explicit session-time check (09:30 to 16:00 bar time) that skips all entry/exit signal evaluation outside that window, implemented via self.data.datetime.datetime(0) without importing the datetime module.
assumptions.reason: The spec explicitly instructs ignoring signals outside regular market hours; implemented literally even though the supplied data is already confined to regular hours.

assumptions.choice: Entries use plain self.buy()/self.sell() with default size per canonical default; the protective StopTrail order is explicitly sized to self.position.size (or its absolute value) to exactly offset the open position.
assumptions.reason: Canonical default #1 governs entry sizing only; a broker-side stop order that isn't self.close() must be given an explicit size to fully flatten the position it protects.
